author: Roque Planas
description:
President directs interior department to display signs outside museum that accuse institution of inaccuracy

Donald Trump on Friday ordered the interior department to display signs in front of the Smithsonian National Museum of American History that accuse the institution of inaccuracy.

The order escalates the Trump’s attacks against the Smithsonian, which he and his allies accuse of politicizing the institution by focusing too much on injustices in American history, instead of more triumphant moments such as the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

Continue reading...
title: Trump escalates Smithsonian attack with order for signs outside history museum

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
President flew to Ankara onboard Qatari-gifted jet, without advanced defenses, and flew home on old Air Force One

Donald Trump switched aircraft before departing Turkey earlier this month after US officials determined there was a credible threat from Iranian proxy forces targeting him and Air Force One, according to a new report from the New York Times.

The threat surfaced while the US president was attending the Nato summit. He had arrived in Ankara onboard the new Qatari-donated Boeing 747-8, an aircraft that Trump acknowledged does not have t
title: Trump switched planes in Turkey earlier this month because of threat from Iran proxy forces – report

author: Richard Luscombe and agency
description:
Colt Gray, who was 14 at time of attack on Apalachee high school, admits 55 charges including four counts of murder

The wife of a teacher killed in a high school shooting in Georgia two years ago told a court on Friday that the families of the four victims had been handed “a life sentence of grief and trauma” by the teenage student who murdered them.

Shayna Aspinwall, whose husband Richard died at Apalachee high school, about 45 miles north-east Atlanta, on 4 September 2024, was speaking at the sentencing hearing for Colt Gray, 16, who earlier pleaded to 55 charges, including second-degree murder.

Continue reading...
title: Georgia school shooter handed victims’ families ‘life sentence of trauma’, court hears

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
DNC move aims to better represent views of party’s racially diverse voter base ahead of next presidential cycle

Democrats moved to keep South Carolina as the first state to vote in their party’s 2028 presidential primary process, while moving up several other states, in an effort to better represent the views of the party’s racially diverse voter base.

At a meeting in Washington DC of the Democratic National Committee’s (DNC) rules and bylaws committee on Friday, South Carolina received a slim majority of votes to take the first spot, scheduled for 22 January 2028, with Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia set to follow, in that order. The selections must still be confirmed by the full DNC at a meeting set for next month.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats move to keep South Carolina as first state to vote in 2028 presidential primaries

author: Roque Planas
description:
Joanna Ruth Shields’ body was found in a pool of water with suspicious marks, driving speculation she was attacked

A young woman whose body was found in the backcountry of California’s Big Sur with suspicious marks on her face and neck died of alcohol withdrawal, the Monterey county sheriff’s office said on Thursday.

The discovery of Joanna Ruth Shields’ body in April had driven widespread suspicion that she had been the victim of a violent attack. A group of hikers found Shields, 37, naked in a pool of water in the Sykes hot springs area of the Ventana wilderness with marks on her neck and a cut across her forehead.

Continue reading...
title: Police say alcohol withdrawal caused woman’s death in California backcountry

author: Kiran Stacey and Patrick Butler
description:
Exclusive: Andy Burnham thought to be considering waiving stricter right to remain rules for people already working in the sector

Hundreds of thousands of care workers could be exempted from the home secretary’s plans to toughen up the immigration system under proposals being considered by Andy Burnham as he looks for ways to relieve pressure on the social care sector.

The prime minister will give a speech next week spelling out his determination to start creating a National Care Service before the next general election as he looks to accelerate the process set up by his predecessor, Keir Starmer.

Continue reading...
title: Existing care workers could be exempt from UK’s tough new immigration rules

author: Hayden Vernon
description:
Metropolitan police say officers on marine policing boat are receiving treatment after incident in central London

Five officers have been injured after a police boat struck Westminster Bridge in central London on Friday afternoon.

The Metropolitan police said the incident occurred at about 3.40pm and involved a boat from the marine policing unit.

Continue reading...
title: Five officers injured as police boat strikes Westminster Bridge

author: Guardian staff and agency
description:
Six migrants from Honduras and Mexico – including 14-year-old boy – were found dead in May near US-Mexico border

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email

A US attorney announced a federal indictment on Friday against 11 people in the smuggling deaths of six migrants whose bodies were found in a rail cargo container in Texas in May.

The six people were found dead in a rail yard shipping container in Laredo, on the US-Mexico bo
title: 11 people indicted over deaths of six people in cargo container in Texas

author: Jasper Jolly
description:
Exclusive: Eight companies expect to be covered by the ban for 2025-26, the Guardian can reveal

Water company bosses’ total pay rose over the past year despite a government bonus ban and public outrage over pollution and bills, the Guardian can reveal.

One chief executive, Mark Thurston of Anglian Water, received £1.9m – including a £500,000 “retention payment”, despite the bonus ban.

Continue reading...
title: Water bosses’ pay rises despite bonus ban and public fury over bills and pollution

author: Alexandra Topping, Political correspondent
description:
‘Daily routine of hit jobs and smears will not deter us from winning next general election,’ party briefing notes say

Reform UK has instructed its councillors to describe a police investigation into donations from the mother of George Cottrell as an establishment stitch-up, as polling showed the party’s popularity plummeting.

Internal briefing documents circulated to the party’s councillors included instructions to respond to questions about a Metropolitan police investigation into party donations with: “It is now clear that the establishment will try anything to stop us”, the Times revealed on Thursday.
title: Reform councillors told to describe donations inquiry as establishment stitch-up

author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
description:
A £10,000 bar tab was drunk, there was a ‘lot of anger’, and now ex-ministers are thinking how to cooperate in future

Keir Starmer’s leaving party had been planned for some time. But in years to come it might be seen as the birth of a new Labour movement.

Dozens of ministers, aides and Starmer himself headed to the Grafton pub in Kentish Town on Monday night to drown their sorrows, hours after the former prime minister left Downing Street for the last time.

Continue reading...
title: Was Keir Starmer’s leaving party the boozy birth of a new Labour force?

author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
description:
Economists’ warning comes as escalating Middle East crisis pushes global crude oil back above $US100 a barrel

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australian households face the prospect of a Reserve Bank interest rate hike and petrol prices above $2 a litre over the coming weeks, economists warn, as the escalating Middle East crisis pushes global crude back above $US100 a barrel.

Financial markets now see an even chance the RBA board will deliver a fourth cash rate increase at the next meeting on 11 August.
title: Australian households face prospect of interest rate hike and petrol prices rising above $2 a litre

author: Ben Smee
description:
The One Nation leader has allied herself with men’s rights activists for years, consistently suggesting women routinely make false allegations of violence

For a decade, Pauline Hanson has been beating the same drum.

Her comments this week – suggesting domestic violence was a “two-way street” <
title: Pauline Hanson’s domestic violence comments were no stumble

author: Ajit Niranjan
description:
The conditions for ferocious fires are expected to worsen as the planet heats up, putting more people at risk

Fierce wildfires after back-to-back heatwaves have forced tens of thousands of people across southern Europe to flee their homes, while powerful infernos across Canada and the US choke big cities with thick smoke.

Continue reading...
title: How dangerous are wildfires and how can we stop them from getting worse?

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Explosive diarrhea infection detected in 41 states with at least 72 sickened by new, as yet unknown source of parasite

Confusion abounds in the cyclospora outbreak that has sickened thousands in at least 41 states, as officials identify a new cluster of cases and more potential products come under scrutiny.

The recall of products during this outbreak of explosive diarrhea has been an unusual one, complicated by poor communication, politicization and the delay of a new regulatory rule could have helped trace the cyclosporiasis outbreak faster.

Continue reading...
title: Confusing product recall adds to US cyclospora outbreak uncertainty

author: PA Media
description:
Warning in place until Sunday morning in southern and central regions after drought declared in parts of Wales

Heat alerts are in place across parts of England, with officials saying temperatures are likely to have an impact on health and wellbeing.

The yellow heat health alerts issued for the East Midlands, east of England, London, south-east, south-west and West Midlands are in place until 9am on Sunday.

Continue reading...
title: Parts of England under heat alert with 30C possible

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
Kagan rejects notion that high court ‘does whatever the administration wants’, pointing to tariffs ruling and more

Liberal justice Elena Kagan has said it was “wrong” to accuse the US supreme court of becoming a rubber stamp for Donald Trump in his second term, amid criticism of its authorization of some of the president’s most controversial actions.

Pointing to rulings against the president on key issues such as tariffs, Kagan – one of three liberals on a court that has in recent years been defined by rulings authored by members of its six-justice conservative majority – defended it at an annual gathering of attorneys and judges for the ninth judicial circuit in Bellevue, Washington, on Thursday.

Continue reading...
title: Justice Elena Kagan decries idea that US supreme court ‘rubber-stamps’ Trump’s agenda

author: Richard Luscombe
description:
Court questions plan to offer male hormone treatment to cisgender troops while denying it to trans service members

Pete Hegseth’s controversial plan to screen older soldiers for testosterone deficiencies and offer them more of the hormone faced scrutiny this week from a federal judge, who ordered the Trump administration to explain a discrepancy with the treatment of transgender troops.

The US defense secretary announced earlier this month that male service members aged 30 and above would be checked to ensure they have the “right testosterone levels” to perform in the military at an optimal level.

Continue reading...
title: Judge orders Hegseth to explain US military’s new testosterone policy

author: Priya Bharadia
description:
Police appeal for witnesses after collision in Huyton leaves four men dead and a fifth in hospital

Four men in their 20s have died after a car crash in Merseyside in the early hours of Friday.

Police were called just before 2am to reports that a black Seat Cupra had left the road and collided with a lamp-post in Huyton. The car was travelling from Liverpool towards Knowsley.

Continue reading...
title: Four men in 20s die after car crashes into lamp-post in Merseyside

author: Associated Press
description:
Sister Leticia Ugboaja says she went into a cold sweat as ICE officers approached her in McAllen on her way to church

A nun who was taken into immigration custody last month in Texas said on Thursday that she went into a cold sweat as two armed men approached her while she walked to Sunday mass in her habit, thinking about the day’s Bible readings and carrying little more than her rosary and cellphone.

“Honestly, in that moment, I did not understand what was going on, what was happening to me,” Sister Leticia Ugboaja said at a news conference at Our Lady of Sorrows church in McAllen, Texas, on the US-Mexico border, where she spoke out for the first time since US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers arreste
title: Texas nun detained by ICE speaks out for first time: ‘It was very heartbreaking for me’

author: Luke Harding in Kyiv and agencies
description:
Rightwing provocateur meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who says he expects talks with Donald Trump in Washington next week

Volodymyr Zelenskyy will meet Donald Trump in Washington next week, according to the rightwing US influencer Laura Loomer, amid signs the White House’s traditional hostility towards Ukraine is beginning to crumble.

In an interview with Loomer, the Ukraine president said he will probably attend Senator Lindsey Graham’s funeral and hold talks with Trump, which will take place as the latest version of the Russian sanctions bill makes its way through Congress.

Continue reading...
title: Maga influencer Laura Loomer reverses course on Ukraine after Kyiv visit

author: Pjotr Sauer
description:
Kyiv’s attacks on Wildberries, country’s answer to Amazon, destroy goods made, sold, and bought by everyday Russians

Standing in front of a vast warehouse engulfed in flames outside Moscow, Tatyana Mikhailova watched as her entire stock of 4,000 fur coats, bought months in advance for the winter season, burned.

“It’s not just a warehouse that’s burning,” Mikhailova said in a video she shared on Instagram. “It’s the time you’ve invested, the immense stress you’ve endured, your money, and your last bit of hope. All I feel is emptiness.”

Continue reading...
title: Ukraine’s pivot to warehouse strikes brings war closer to ordinary Russians

author: Gaya Gupta and Guardian staff
description:
US president faced criticism after officials announced tariffs of between 10% and 12.5% on more than 80 countries

  • US politics live – latest updates

Donald Trump has been accused of using forced labor as “a pretext” to impose a fresh wave of tariffs on dozens of countries, as critics warned of higher prices for Americans.

The US president faced swift criticism from Democrats after his officials presented their latest effort to make his signature economic policy permanent following a string of high-profile legal setbacks. Some Republicans also expressed concern.
title: Democrats accuse Trump of using forced labor as ‘convenient’ justification for tariffs

author: Katie McQue in New York
description:
Residents warn project could worsen gambling addiction and raise rents, while developers promise jobs

On Main Street in Flushing’s Chinatown, shoppers weave between fruit stands, restaurants and family-run businesses that have served the New York City neighborhood for decades. But behind the bustle, many residents fear the working-class immigrant community is under threat from an $8bn casino development that could displace thousands of renters and force small businesses to close.

“A predatory project is being dumped in our community that disproportionately harms our people,” said Jack Hu, 37, a Flushing resident and member of the No Casino in Flushing Meadows Corona Park campaign. “This community is really upset about this project and how it was pushed through without our consent.”

Continue reading...
title: New York Chinatown fears impact of $8bn casino development, calling it ‘predatory project’

description:
Even some Republicans apparently expressing concern over measures against 85 countries

  • What to know about Trump’s new tariffs on more than 80 countries

  • Sign up for the US Breaking News email

President Donald Trump ⁠will address the White House Correspondents’ Association at a rescheduled dinner later today, nearly three months after a shooting at the Washington Hilton hotel interrupted the event.

The black-tie gathering of journalists, politicians and administration officials ⁠was called off on 25 ⁠April after a ​man tried to force his way through a secu
title: Trump’s new tariffs ‘a sales tax that will make life harder for Americans’, say Democrats – US politics live

author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
description:
While overall levy for UK is unchanged, sectors not covered by Turnberry deal face tougher competition

  • Business live – latest updates

Donald Trump’s latest round of tariffs has put UK businesses at a disadvantage against the EU even though the overall tariff for British goods has not changed, experts have said.

In the levies, announced late on Thursday and said to be aimed against countries that engage in forced labour, the EU’s previous 15% near blanket tariff is reduced to 10%, the same level as the tariff deal struck by Keir Starmer and Peter Mandelson last year.

Continue reading...
title: Trump’s latest tariffs put UK at disadvantage to EU, say experts

author: Nicola Slawson
description:
Measures replace 10% global duty and come after supreme court declared many of the earlier tariffs illegal. Plus, how secondhand fashion got so expensive

Good morning.

Donald Trump has imposed a fresh round of tariffs on more than 80 countries to replace a 10% global duty that was due to expire, provoking a wave of criticism and protests from US allies and trading partners.

What is Trump’s justification for the tariffs? The newest tariffs, announced late last night by the US trade representative, Jamieson Greer, would fall under section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974, aimed against countries that engage in forced labor. Trump had said his administration would investigate unfair trading practices to impose permanent tariffs as soon as the February supreme court decision was announced.

How have the affected countries
title: First Thing: Trump imposes fresh tariffs on UK, EU and dozens of other trading partners

author: Robert Tait in Washington
description:
Journalists urge attenders to confront president over media attacks, while Melanie Trump and JD Vance to be absent

Donald Trump will address a rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Association (WCHA) dinner on Friday three months after the original event was abruptly halted after an armed assailant tried to storm it, with the alleged aim of assassinating him.

The rearranged dinner has been condemned as “hypocritical” by retired journalists and press freedom groups, who are urging the association to use it to confront Trump over his administration’s intensified attacks on the media.

Continue reading...
title: Trump to speak at White House press dinner rescheduled after shooting

author: Taz Ali
description:
PM will chair the inaugural meeting of the national economic council that will aim to shift economic decision-making away ‌from London

Heavy police presence this morning outside Heron House in central Manchester, where the prime minister will hold his first meeting at No 10 North:

Consumer confidence in the UK jumped this month by its biggest margin for nearly three years as the prospect of Andy Burnham becoming prime minister became almost certain.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham to spend first working day at new No 10 North in Manchester – UK politics live

author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent
description:
‘Intense and highly unpredictable’ blaze forces more than 40,000 people to flee popular holiday spot

  • Europe live – latest updates

Authorities in south-western France have ordered the total evacuation of the Cap Ferret peninsula on the Atlantic coast by land and sea as an “intense and highly unpredictable” wildfire advances on one of the country’s best-known holiday spots.

The fire had burned more than 10,000 hectares (24,700 acres) by Friday morning, the French interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, said, with 40,000 people already or about to be evacuated, including thousands of tourists from campsites and rental homes.

Continue reading...
title: France orders total evacuation of Cap Ferret peninsula as wildfire spreads

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Inquiry’s focus this week is on security for the Jewish community, with the MP telling the commissioner his son is afraid to attend synagogues and events

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The shadow education minister, Julian Leeser, has called for universities to undertake an audit of any classes that teach about the Jewish community, Israel or Palestine.

Appearing before the royal commission into antisemitism and social cohesion on Friday, Leeser said he had been “very concerned” about antisemitism on university campuses and was not satisfied with how vice-chancellors had addressed the issue after the 7 Octob
title: University courses covering Israel-Palestine should be audited, Julian Leeser tells royal commission

author: Mark Sweney and agencies
description:
Measures effectively replace blanket 10% tariffs Trump imposed in February that were struck down by US supreme court

Donald Trump has once again inspired anger and confusion in US allies and trading partners as he imposed a wave of tariffs on more than 80 countries, replacing an expiring global duty introduced earlier this year.

The new measures effectively replace blanket 10% tariffs that Trump imposed in February. The US supreme court ruled many of those were illegal. The new levies come in at between 10% and 12.5% on countries including the UK, Mexico, Canada, Australia, India, China and the 27 countries that make up the EU.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Forced labour’ rationale for Trump tariffs met with bewilderment

author: Mark Sweney
description:
Hot weather and World Cup fever help defy analyst expectations of decline, with sales volumes up 1% in June

Online sales accounted for the highest level of retail sales in five years last month as record hot weather spurred a rush for air conditioning, outdoor products and clothing.

The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said the volume of retail sales in Great Britain grew 1% month on month in June, as the hot weather and a World Cup retail rush defied analyst expectations of a 0.3% decline.

Continue reading...
title: Heatwave and online shopping drive up retail sales in Great Britain

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Evacuees have been told to leave the area before 10am, using hundreds of mobilised boats or the only road linking the area with the mainland

Thousands of people have been forced to flee parts of south-west France amid worsening wildfires that prompted the authorities to order people to evacuate from the Cap Ferret peninsula along the Atlantic coast.

Evacuees have been told to leave the area before 10am, using hundreds of mobilised boats or the only road linking the area with the mainland.

Continue reading...
title: France orders evacuation of Cap Ferret peninsula as wildfire spreads – Europe live

author: Achol Arok
description:
TGA says product information for some diabetes and weight loss drugs updated with warning of NAION disorder

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s medicines regulator has issued warnings for several type 2 diabetes and obesity-related treatments – including Ozempic and Mounjaro – over the potential to cause a “rare but severe” eye disorder that could lead to blindness.

The Therapeutic Goods Administration’s (TGA)
title: Australian regulator TGA warns of ‘rare but severe’ eye disorder linked to GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic

author: Rob Davies
description:
Landlords say high costs of running hospitality business outweigh potential savings of business rates discount

One of Andy Burnham’s first policy measures as prime minister is a 20% reduction in business rates for pubs, clubs and live music venues.

The policy, announced on Thursday, is part of a broader agenda to support the high street and will cost £100m.

Continue reading...
title: ‘A small snippet’: what pubs make of Burnham’s £100m rates giveaway

author: Graham Readfearn Environment and climate correspondent
description:
Digital billboards from environmental groups, targeting Labor MPs attending national conference, cancelled with airport stating they are ‘too political’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Conservation groups have questioned why their advertisements targeting Labor politicians were pulled by Adelaide airport for breaking rules on political advertising while others promoting gas and mining kept running.

Labor politicians including the prime minister, Anthony
title: Adelaide airport pulls ads from conservation groups but keeps gas and mining ads during ALP conference

author: Christopher Knaus
description:
Edmund Rice Education Australia can be sued over abuse committed by Catholic order, after receiving much of its property holdings

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The entity gifted vast property holdings by the Christian Brothers has agreed to help compensate abuse survivors in full, in a stunning reversal after weeks of public pressure.

The Christian Brothers, a Catholic order with a long history of clergy abuse,
title: Christian Brothers abuse victims to get ‘full’ compensation in backdown after controversial property sales

author: Stephanie Convery
description:
Marat Ganiev, 55, fails in attempt to permanently halt remaining charge of perverting the course of justice

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The man previously charged with killing 19-year-old Melbourne woman Isla Bell has failed in his attempt to have the final charge against him relating to her death thrown out.

Marat Ganiev, 55, was initially charged with the murder of Bell after her remains were found in a bag in a Dandenong rubbish tip on 20 November 2024, about six weeks after the night police believe she died.

Continue reading...
title: Isla Bell death: man previously accused of killing Melbourne teen loses bid to have final charge dropped

author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Hannah Ellis-Petersen; produced by Saskia Collette, Alex Atack and Brian McNamara; executive producer Eli Block
description:
South Asia correspondent Hannah Ellis-Petersen on the Cockroach movement – and the students driving India’s biggest protests in years

‘I’ve never seen this many young people out on the streets,’ says Hannah Ellis-Petersen.

For days, tens of thousands of Indians have been marching under the banner of the Cockroach Janta party.

Continue reading...
title: The ‘cockroaches’ marching on India’s government – podcast

author: Gaya Gupta
description:
Tariffs ranging from 10%-12.5%, taking effect on Friday, are US president’s latest effort to circumvent Congress

Just before a temporary levy on global imports was set to expire, the Trump administration issued a fresh wave of tariffs on more than 80 countries late on Thursday, ranging from 10% to 12.5%. The new tariffs take effect Friday morning.

It’s Donald Trump’s latest effort to continue imposing global levies without congressional approval, despite the supreme court ruling in February that found the US president had illegally used his executive power to implement his global trade policies. Trump has long maintained that the US has been paying more than its fair share in tariffs, and that increased duties are necessary to boost American manufacturing and jobs.

Continue reading...
title: What to know about Trump’s new tariffs on more than 80 countries

author: Robert Mackey
description:
New York Times reports that list of those killed changed from 18 on Wednesday to 14 on Thursday

The Pentagon’s official online list of service members killed in the ongoing Iran war does not include the four soldiers who died during renewed fighting over the weekend, despite the fact that their names were included in a Pentagon press release on the formal transfer of their remains back to the United States on Wednesday.

A review of the current list on the Pentagon’s Defense Casualty Analysis System website shows that, despite having been last updated on Wednesday, the number of US military personnel killed during Operation Epic Fury, the Pentagon’s name for the US-Israeli war on Iran that Donald Trump launched on 28 February, remains at 14.
title: Pentagon list of service members killed in Iran war removes most recent four

author: Roque Planas
description:
Suspect allegedly yelled ‘Allahu Akbar’ before attacking a 57-year-old Asian man and a 50-year-old Jewish man

New York City police are investigating a pair of stabbings near Central Park as a possible hate crime, police commissioner Jessica Tisch said Thursday.

The suspect, Raul Morales, allegedly stabbed a 57-year-old Asian man in the back with a knife, then stabbed a 50-year-old Jewish man in the torso with a screwdriver, according to a New York police department spokesperson. Morales allegedly yelled “Allahu Akbar” before the stabbings, police said. The attacks occurred about two blocks apart and in broad daylight in Manhattan’s affluent Upper West Side neighborhood.

Continue reading...
title: Double stabbing in New York City being investigated as possible hate crime
